name: UA Client Hints, low entropy
plain: Browser brand list, mobile flag and OS name that Chromium sends by default.
meaning: Three coarse hints (Sec-CH-UA, Sec-CH-UA-Mobile, Sec-CH-UA-Platform) replace most of the old User-Agent. They split the audience into mobile vs desktop and Windows vs macOS vs Android with almost no tracking power.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: brands
fields.range: 3 or so brand+version pairs incl. one randomized GREASE brand like Not A;Brand

fields.name: platform
fields.range: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, Chrome OS, iOS(n/a), Unknown

limits.headline: Can see your browser brand, whether it is mobile, and your OS name
limits.user_action: Nothing. Chromium sends this with every request
can: See a yes or no for mobile
See whether you use Windows, macOS, Android, or Linux
Split visitors into big groups, such as mobile and desktop
cannot: See exact versions or device models
Work in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
Tell you apart from many other visitors
See your name, location, or accounts
limits.differs: Chromium browsers send them. Firefox and Safari send the old user agent text instead.

story.what_it_is: Three basic facts sent by default: browser brand, phone or not, and operating system name.

marketing.name: User-Agent Client Hints
marketing.pitch: Chrome sends a short default set and lets sites ask for more, as part of reducing the old user agent.

story.for_you: You never see these. They ride along with every page request, in the background. They let a site know if you are on a phone or a computer so it shows the right version.
story.for_makers: These replace most of the old user agent. They give just enough to serve mobile or desktop pages and basic OS fixes. They are coarse, so they carry less tracking value.

use_cases.example: A shop sends a mobile layout to phones and a full layout to desktops from the very first request.
A game portal picks the mobile or desktop version of a browser game before the page loads.
A news site routes phones to a lightweight version of an article.
A video site chooses a mobile player on phones and a full player on computers.
A traffic dashboard splits visits into mobile and desktop and Windows, Mac and Android.
A bot tool compares the brand list with other signals and flags a fake Chrome.

technical_bounds: Chromium family only (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave)
Brand list order and GREASE token are randomized per version to stop sniffing

history.change: Sec-CH-UA, Mobile, Platform sent by default on HTTPS
UA string reduction completes the shift of detail to hints
